title: Keep world arrival responsive while procedural planet baking warms in

scope.subject: Preserve the existing YEIS destination/Approach contract while moving expensive procedural planet baking behind an immediate usable fallback

research_summary: Cloud Playwright traces show exact Earth destination resolution completes and identifies yeis-planet:earth, but the visible Approach arrival can remain unobservable for many seconds after the state handoff. The already-adopted ProceduralPlanets documentation explicitly states that bakePlanet cost scales with textureSize/meshResolution and blocks the GPU while it runs, recommending baking during loading. Keep the existing YEIS/R3F destination and scene stack, render the current lightweight fallback immediately, and schedule the already-integrated baked representation only after the arrival frame has had a chance to commit. This fixes product responsiveness without introducing a second renderer, navigation authority or planet visual system.

sources.finding: The verified MIT YEIS snapshot remains the selected full universe/navigation backbone; body identity and cross-scale destination semantics should not be replaced to solve a rendering-arrival stall.
React Three Fiber is already the host renderer lifecycle and shared Canvas, so the fix should stay inside the existing scene lifecycle rather than add a parallel WebGL surface.

ProceduralPlanets documents that bakePlanet can take milliseconds to seconds depending on textureSize and meshResolution, blocks the GPU while running, and should be performed during loading; its baked output is already the adopted ordinary-world representation.

React documents separating urgent UI updates from non-critical work and reusing memoized/effect primitives; the product can keep arrival feedback urgent while scheduling the existing visual bake as non-critical follow-up work.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the verified MIT YEIS backbone and its body/Approach semantics; the observed defect is rendering responsiveness after resolution, not a missing universe or navigation product.
Reuse the existing R3F Canvas lifecycle so fallback and baked representations stay in one scene and one camera stack.
Keep ProceduralPlanets as the adopted ordinary-world renderer, but use its documented baking cost as a loading concern instead of blocking the first observable arrival.
Use the React primitives already in the bundle for a small scheduling/lifecycle adapter; no new scheduler or loading framework is warranted.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS product arrival backbone
candidates.source: Existing Personal Universe YEIS destination and Approach integration
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned e520568 plus retained third-party notices
candidates.reason: Retains the authoritative body identity, system resolution and Approach semantics; it does not by itself prevent the separate baked planet renderer from occupying the GPU after arrival.

candidates.name: Existing React Three Fiber scene lifecycle
candidates.source: Current shared Canvas and component lifecycle
candidates.reason: Provides the existing single renderer and lifecycle boundary needed to show the lightweight fallback first and mount the baked world later without a second scene.

candidates.name: ProceduralPlanets baked world behind progressive fallback
candidates.source: Already-integrated bakePlanet subsystem with its documented loading boundary
candidates.reason: Preserves the adopted visual subsystem and deterministic world appearance while moving its documented expensive bake behind the already-present fallback instead of replacing it.

candidates.name: React effect/ref scheduling glue
candidates.reason: Enough for a bounded cancellation-safe deferred bake handoff; adding another task scheduler or loading framework would add authority without removing the GPU-bound bake cost.

decision.rationale: Keep the full YEIS/R3F product stack and the already-adopted ProceduralPlanets visual subsystem. The only new code is narrow scheduling/cancellation glue that lets the lightweight fallback and Approach UI commit before the GPU-blocking bake begins, preserving the correct Earth product-world contract instead of weakening the test into native fallback travel.
decision.fallback: If deferred baking still causes unacceptable interaction stalls, reduce non-high texture resolution or keep the fallback longer before considering a different planet renderer; do not change navigation identity to hide rendering latency.
